submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad query-gated previous-token head: the current word's query controls attention back to the previous token (gradable adjectives after how/what attend it at ~0.9 while pronouns and nouns mostly self-attend), so ordinary multi-word prose is active-weak (peaks 0.25-0.4x scale) and strong peaks (>=0.4x) occur only on the second word of a tight left-licensing pair: a gradable adjective/adverb after how/what (how good/much/well/often), a bare verb after infinitival to or a preverbal quantifier (to compensate, Both were), a gerund after When (When running), a plural noun after a numeral/quantifier (two sides, both directions, either side), or a content noun after what (what values/precautions). Non-licensing continuations are locally weak (how it/the, the + noun, verb + how), and only single-word/interjection texts, bare numeric strings, and short probes with no licensing pair stay fully below the line.

rival_explanations: Pure previous-token identity head: strength is set by the previous token's value alone (how/what/When/Both/to/two all write far-from-mean vectors), so how it should peak as strongly as how good.

Sentence/clause-onset position head: fires on words in early linear positions (first content word of a sentence or clause) regardless of the licensing relation, so any sentence-initial content word should peak strongly and mid-sentence licensing pairs should not.
